title: Incremental Response Federation API notes
content:
Context and intent:

This is a personal design scratch for an "incremental response federation" pattern: allow a client to concurrently consume and merge partial generative outputs from multiple Redwood endpoints (hosted + dedicated/private) with deterministic merge semantics, resumability, and cost-awareness. The goal is a small client API surface that: 
- supports multiplexed partial chunks from heterogeneous backends
- defines a merge strategy that is repeatable (replayable) given the same event stream
- helps clients gracefully fall back to cheaper/cached sources mid-stream
- provides hooks for telemetry and local heuristics (latency/cost thresholds)

Constraints / real-world scenarios:
- mobile SDK with intermittent connectivity (need deterministic resume)
- enterprise app with private model + fallback to hosted for coverage
- aggregated responses for multi-turn chat where parts come from different skill models

High-level model:
- Producer endpoints emit chunked events with globally unique stream ids (uuid4) and monotonically increasing chunk_index ints.
- Events include a lightweight provenance header (source, model_version, generation_config_id).
- Client maintains a small WAL (append-only) of received events for resumption/replay. Events are idempotent.
- Merge pipeline on client maps events into final tokens/text using strategy layers: token-wise merge -> segment merge -> policy postprocess.

Wire shape (event stream event = JSON line):
{
  "stream_id": "uuid4",
  "chunk_index": 0,
  "type": "delta",            // delta | metadata | end | error
  "payload": "text fragment or token array",
  "cursor_hint": 0,          // optional token index into full seq for alignment heuristics
  "provenance": "hosted:us-west-2/model-x:v2",
  "confidence": 0.87,        // optional numeric, used by merge policy
  "timestamp": "2025-03-05T15:12:34Z"
}

API surfaces (client-facing):
1) startStream (client->controller):
- body: { request_id, prompt, prefer_sources: ["private", "dedicated", "hosted"], resume_after_stream_id? }
- response: { stream_id, endpoints: [{url, token, model_profile}] }
- controller will return one or more endpoint URLs to connect via websocket/SSE/HTTP2 stream.

2) onEvent (event stream):
- client subscribes to SSE/WS. Events are JSON lines (see wire shape). Client must ack critical events (end/error) to controller to avoid double work.

3) resumeStream:
- client sends 'resume' with last_known_chunk_index and last_event_hash list. Controller can decide which endpoints to re-issue or switch to cached result.

Merge strategies (configurable):
- first-writer-wins: accept earliest complete token for each cursor position
- highest-confidence: prefer payloads with higher provided confidence values, tie-break by latency
- stitched: accept non-overlapping segments, requires cursor_hint from producer
- policy: user-defined JS-like function evaluated locally for complex merging

Edge cases to handle:
- overlapping deltas (same cursor positions with different tokens)
- truncated streams: endpoint sends end before enough content; client can request 'fill' from fallback endpoint
- divergent replays: after resume, two endpoints may produce different continuations. Need deterministic conflict resolution rule (e.g., choose source priority list + stable hashing of remaining prompt).

Client WAL format (append-only line-delimited JSON):
- lines: event_json + newline; small cap (e.g., max 256KB per stream) and checkpoint policy to compress older events into snapshot {text:..., merged_cursor}. Snapshot entries are single-line base64 blobs.

Operational knobs to expose in SDK:
- source_priority: e.g., ["private", "dedicated", "hosted"]
- merge_policy: "first-writer-wins" | "highest-confidence" | custom_fn_id
- resume_window: seconds to allow resume attempts (default 300s)
- wal_sync: sync-on-ack | periodic (fractional seconds)
- telemetry_sample_rate: e.g., 0.05 (to limit PII-sensitive traces)

Controller responsibilities (server-side):
- maintain ephemeral routing map for stream_id -> endpoints + token TTL
- dedupe replayed resume requests via last_event_hash set
- accept client acks and optionally reconcile billing attribution (which endpoint served which chunks)
- provide a compact stream proof (hash chain) clients can store to validate continuity after resume

Security and privacy notes:
- do not include PII in unencrypted telemetry. Provide redact hooks.
- provenance header should be minimal (region/model-tag) and avoid tenant-identifying IPs.

Telemetry ideas for first-pass metric collection:
- latency_percentiles per endpoint (10/50/90/99) as observed by clients
- merge_conflict_rate per app/version
- resume_success_rate + resumed_duplicate_events_rate
- cost_attribution by chunk (approx tokens * endpoint_unit_cost)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should the controller be authoritative for conflict resolution, or leave fully client-side deterministic rules?
  - tradeoff: server can enforce consistent finalization but adds latencies and coupling
- Are token-level alignments too expensive for mobile clients? maybe restrict to segment alignment and provide optional tokenization hints from server.
- Persistent storage model for WAL snapshots (local encrypted store vs OS-backed keystore).
- How to represent function/tool calls mid-stream? special event type 'tool_call' + structured payload?

Prototype quicknotes:
- implement a minimal local SDK that uses SSE with a small in-memory WAL, first-writer-wins policy and resume by re-requesting controller for endpoints.
- integration test: simulate private endpoint that artificially pauses and then resumes with slightly different continuation; verify deterministic merge rule stability.

Example debugging trace (for devs):
- client logs: [stream:uuid4] recv chunk 0 from hosted (lat 120ms) -> append WAL
- recv chunk 0 from private (lat 50ms) -> merge first-writer-wins kept private -> ack chunk 0 to controller
- private sends end -> client sees gap -> controller returns hosted 'fill' endpoint -> client requests fill and merges

References and related internal tickets:
- INC-342 (partial merge semantics): https://linear.app/RED/issue/INC-342-partial-merge
- runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1284

Notes to self:
- keep wire minimal and opt-in for heavy alignment payloads.
- prioritize developer ergonomics: simple start/resume/stop primitives, sensible defaults for mobile.
- follow up with SRE for cost attribution ideas before prototyping 'per-chunk' billing metadata.

-- end --
